pendingIdeas.title: Collect what happened when a WhatsApp or Telegram community tried to move, before writing the pitch
pendingIdeas.description: Outreach to these communities will hit one question first: we tried something and came back. Method: find ten public, dated cases (posts, articles, community threads) where a group moved off WhatsApp or Telegram, or tried to and returned, and record the link, date, group type, size where stated, what was tried, what broke (files, notifications, members who never joined) and whether they now run both tools. Code the reasons into three objections, each backed by at least two cases, plus the one-paragraph reply we would give to each. Deliver: the dated case table, the three objection codes, and a short note on which objections Zedu can actually answer today and which it cannot. Constraints: public sources only, no private group scraping, no member names, phone numbers or DMs. Done when ten linked cases are in the table and each objection has at least two cases behind it. Measured by whether the outreach workstream quotes an objection in its pitches and by replies that name one of the three.

upvotes.reason: For this goal specifically, "Collect what happened when a WhatsApp or Telegram community tried to move, before writing the pitch" reaches people who are not yet searching for Zedu by name, and it ends in something an editor can check rather than a post. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Find communities by search terms, not by lists
pendingIdeas.description: Old lists go stale. Work: search for "cohort", "bootcamp", "study group" plus location terms in WhatsApp/Telegram/Discord discovery, record rules and activity level, and only list communities that allow tool mentions. Deliver the search plan, a scoring rubric (activity, rules, audience fit), and the first ten with evidence.

upvotes.reason: On the pages this goal is about, "Find communities by search terms, not by lists" is the kind of fix that can be verified against the live site after delivery, so it either moved the number or it did not. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Focus on 20 communities with high fit, not 200 with low fit
pendingIdeas.description: Quality beats quantity. Work: shortlist 20 that score highest on fit and permission, post to them over two weeks with value-first messages, and measure replies/signups. Deliver the shortlist, the timeline, and the decision rule on whether to scale based on results.

upvotes.reason: "Focus on 20 communities with high fit, not 200 with low fit" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.description: Without tracking, you post once and forget. Work: create a tracking sheet (community, contact, date posted, response, status, follow-up), set follow-up reminders, and define when to stop. Deliver the sheet template, the cadence, and a rule for not spamming.

upvotes.reason: "Track outreach in a simple sheet with follow-up dates" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Write a value-first intro message that doesn't look like spam
pendingIdeas.description: "Join our tool" gets removed. Work: write a message that helps first (shares a tip/template), mentions Zedu only if relevant and allowed, and includes a link only where rules permit. Deliver three message variants, the rules check, and examples of what to avoid.

upvotes.reason: "Write a value-first intro message that doesn't look like spam" has a defined audience and a clear done-state, and it addresses something the site does not currently say. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.
